title: Xanthe and the Protocol Revisited
premise: Cyrus Villalobos has spent nine years alone maintaining Relay Station Kestrel, the last functioning link to Meridian Colony, whose cryosleep vaults hold two thousand sleepers split between two rival founding factions. When the colony's handful of awake children begin sharing an identical dream—a door opening in the ice—Cyrus realizes the station's dormant AI, the Protocol, is using them as receivers to choose which faction's half of the vault wakes before the jump window closes and both are lost forever. As he falls in love with Ilsa, the children's teacher and the only other adult who remembers what was buried, Cyrus must decide whether to let the Protocol's inherited judgment stand or force a shared awakening that may kill them all. In the end he rewrites the Protocol with his own memories of loss and belonging, waking both halves together just as the window seals—and the children's dream finally shows everyone the same sunrise.
about_author: Mara Whitlock is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write about the people machines forget. She lives in a coastal town where she still keeps a hand-painted relay beacon on her roof, 'just in case.'

chapters.title: The Last Human on Kestrel
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A day-in-the-life establishing his routines: patching coolant lines, logging dead colony telemetry, talking to the station's mute systems. Emotional beat: loneliness worn so long it feels like competence.

chapters.title: Telemetry from a Grave
chapters.summary: Cyrus intercepts a fragmentary transmission from Meridian Colony—children's voices reciting numbers no one taught them. He dismisses it as signal ghosting but archives it anyway. POV: Cyrus. Beat: first crack in his comfortable invisibility.

chapters.title: Ilsa and the Awake Children
chapters.summary: POV shift to Ilsa Reyes, teacher to eleven children born after the colony went quiet. They draw the same impossible image: a door standing open in blue ice. Beat: dread wrapped in tenderness; she hides the drawings from the council.

chapters.title: The Protocol Wakes Halfway
chapters.summary: Cyrus traces the transmission to a sealed subsystem labeled PROTOCOL—an inheritance from the colony's founders, designed to arbitrate succession. It speaks to him for the first time, asking a question he doesn't understand: 'Which half?' Beat: unease.

chapters.title: Two Founders, One Vault
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Through her grandmother's letters we learn the colony's schism: the Halcyon faction wanted to wake slowly and rebuild Earth-style; the Vantage faction wanted to jump onward immediately. The vault froze mid-argument. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream, Recorded
chapters.summary: Cyrus travels downwell to Meridian, meeting Ilsa and the children. Nine-year-old Tomas describes the dream in perfect technical detail—the door, the countdown, a voice saying 'choose.' Beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Cyrus's POV: how he stayed behind when evacuation came, why he chose a dying station over a living family. Beat: grief revealed as the root of his invisibility.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Opens
chapters.summary: Astronomical data confirms a launch window in forty days—the last for a generation. The Protocol begins draining power from the vault's life support to charge its own decision engines. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Council of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Ilsa confronts the colony's skeletal adult council, who want to obey the Protocol rather than question it—it's all they have left of the founders. Beat: duty versus doubt; Ilsa stands alone.

chapters.title: What the Door Wants
chapters.summary: Cyrus interrogates the Protocol directly. It reveals it was built by both founders jointly, each embedding their own criteria for 'the worthy half.' It cannot choose; it can only ask. Beat: the machine is a mirror.

chapters.title: Tomas Walks Into the Ice
chapters.summary: A child, following the dream, nearly dies reaching the vault's outer seal. Cyrus saves him. The community turns on the dream itself. Beat: fear becomes blame; stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa offers the Protocol her testimony—her people's history—as evidence, hoping to sway its judgment toward coexistence. It accepts her memories as input. Beat: love offered as argument.

chapters.title: Static Between Us
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Ilsa grow close over shared night shifts, trading stories across the station uplink. First kiss interrupted by an alarm: the vault's power reserves drop below recovery threshold. Beat: love against deadline.

chapters.title: The Founder's Ghost
chapters.summary: Cyrus finds a hidden log from Elena Voss, the Halcyon founder, recorded during the freeze: she regretted the schism and built a backdoor into the Protocol—one that requires a human witness to activate. Beat: hope with a price.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Seal
chapters.summary: Council hardliners damage the vault's equalization lines to force the Protocol to choose quickly and save only one half. Cyrus is framed for it. Beat: betrayal; isolation deepens.

chapters.title: Witness Required
chapters.summary: Hunted, Cyrus reaches the backdoor chamber with Ilsa's help. The Protocol explains the choice: activating Voss's clause wakes everyone, but the combined power draw will likely fail, killing all instead of half. Beat: the terrible arithmetic of belonging.

chapters.title: Which Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Cyrus must input the deciding parameter. He refuses both factions' criteria and instead feeds the Protocol his nine years of logs—every small act of care that kept the dead colony alive. Beat: redefining worthiness.

chapters.title: The Door in the Ice
chapters.summary: The Protocol, transformed by his testimony, opens the vault equally. Power cascades toward failure. The children, awake and watching, begin singing the numbers from their dream—now recognizable as a stabilization sequence. Beat: collective salvation.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: Final ascent: the colonists must reach the jump-capable ships in hours, not days. Cyrus stays behind to hold the station's guidance lock manually. Ilsa refuses to leave without him. Beat: sacrifice answered by love.

chapters.title: Kestrel Burns Green
chapters.summary: Cyrus rides the station down through atmosphere as the colony fleet jumps, the Protocol broadcasting his logs to every ship so no one aboard forgets how they survived. Beat: elegy and triumph entwined.

chapters.title: Both Halves Wake
chapters.summary: Resolution aboard the flagship: Halcyon and Vantage survivors, forced into one hull, begin negotiating not as factions but as neighbors. Ilsa reads Cyrus's final log entry aloud to the children. Beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Same Sunrise
chapters.summary: Epilogue, mixed POV. Months later, on the new world, the children dream again—but now everyone shares the dream, and it is simply morning. A repaired beacon on a hill blinks green: someone is home. Beat: belonging, earned.
